prompt: Temi's analog clock, shown here, has an hour hand of length 9 in and a minute hand of length 15 in. When Temi's clock strikes 3 o'clock, what is the length of the segment drawn from the end of the minute hand to the end of the hour hand? Express your answer in simplest radical form.

solutions.title: Pythagorean theorem
solutions.body:
At 3:00 the hands are perpendicular, so the segment is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 9 and 15: $\sqrt{81 + 225} = \sqrt{306} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 34} = 3\sqrt{34}$ in.

**Answer: $3\sqrt{34}$ inches**

solutions.title: Factor first
solutions.body:
$9 = 3 \cdot 3$ and $15 = 3 \cdot 5$, so the triangle is 3 times a 3-5 right triangle, whose hypotenuse is $\sqrt{34}$. Hence $3\sqrt{34}$.

**Answer: $3\sqrt{34}$ inches**

prompt: Kari has an analog clock, shown here, with a minute hand of length 12 in. When Kari's clock strikes 2 o'clock, the segment drawn from the end of the minute hand to the end of the hour hand forms a right triangle with the two hands (as shown). What is the area of this right triangle? Express your answer in simplest radical form.

solutions.title: 30-60-90 triangle
solutions.body:
At 2:00 the hands are $2 \times 30° = 60°$ apart. The right angle is at the tip of the hour hand, so the minute hand (12 in) is the hypotenuse of a 30-60-90 triangle. The hour hand, next to the 60° angle, is the short leg: 6 in. The other leg is $6\sqrt3$ in. Area $= \frac12 \cdot 6 \cdot 6\sqrt3 = 18\sqrt3$ in².

**Answer: $18\sqrt{3}$ square inches**

solutions.title: Area with sine
solutions.body:
Area $= \frac12 \cdot (\text{hour hand}) \cdot (\text{minute hand}) \cdot \sin 60°$. The hour hand is $12\cos 60° = 6$, so area $= \frac12 \cdot 6 \cdot 12 \cdot \frac{\sqrt3}{2} = 18\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $18\sqrt{3}$ square inches**

prompt: Mitch practices playing the violin every evening for 1 hour and 45 minutes. What is the positive difference between the total degrees traveled by the minute hand and the total degrees traveled by the hour hand of an analog clock during Mitch's practice? Express your answer as a decimal to the nearest tenth.

solutions.title: Degrees per minute
solutions.body:
The minute hand turns $360° \div 60 = 6°$ per minute; the hour hand $360° \div 720 = 0.5°$ per minute. In 105 minutes: $630°$ and $52.5°$. Difference: $577.5°$.

**Answer: 577.5 degrees**

solutions.title: Relative speed
solutions.body:
The minute hand gains $6 - 0.5 = 5.5°$ per minute on the hour hand, so in 105 minutes it travels $5.5 \times 105 = 577.5°$ more.

**Answer: 577.5 degrees**
